solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Thick liquid drowning one in hotel lift

parts.note: thick in the sense of stupid, as is dumb in American usage

indicators.note: one thing drowning in another is submerged inside it, so these letters go into the liquid

parts.note: water is the commonest liquid
the Roman numeral for one is I

explanation.surface: Something viscous engulfs a guest riding the hotel elevator.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Thick liquid' looks like one phrase meaning syrup or sludge, but the words work separately; 'drowning' puts the one inside the liquid.
explanation.definitionFit: A small service elevator carrying food or dishes between floors, as in a hotel kitchen, goes by this name.

clue.text: Climbing mount in African country — not South African

indicators.note: one piece sits in the other
not South tells us to drop the S abbreviation from the country

parts.note: Sudan is an African country

indicators.note: in a down clue, climbing means the word for mount is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a nag is a horse, something ridden or mounted

explanation.surface: Some ascent of a mountain in an unnamed African nation, apparently outside South Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: 'African country' looks like one phrase, but African alone is the definition; the country loses its S before 'in' puts it around the reversed mount.
explanation.definitionFit: A person from Uganda is described with this adjective, which is a particular kind of African.

clue.text: Fawn in tropical grass loves leaving island

indicators.note: the loves leaving the grass means those letters go

parts.note: bamboo is a giant grass of tropical regions
love is zero in tennis, written O, so two loves are OO

explanation.surface: A young deer lurks in tropical grassland, which lovers abandon for an island.
explanation.walkthrough: Fawn looks like a colour or a verb meaning to flatter; it is a young deer.
explanation.definitionFit: The Disney film character of that name is a young deer, so he is a famous example of a fawn.

clue.text: Completely grisly setting for end of Poe story

indicators.note: the grisly word is set beside the last letter, following it

parts.note: all as in all done, completely done

indicators.note: end of picks the final letter of the writer's name

parts.note: grisly and gory both describe something bloody and horrid

explanation.surface: Edgar Allan Poe's tale ends in a thoroughly gruesome scene.
explanation.definitionFit: An allegory is a tale whose characters and events carry a hidden moral or political meaning.

clue.text: Grating sounds ruin Attic drama

indicators.note: grating means shredding, so the letters of these three words are torn up and rebuilt

explanation.surface: Harsh noises spoil a play from ancient Athens.
explanation.walkthrough: Attic suggests ancient Greece, but the play is Shakespeare's Roman tragedy.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the title of Shakespeare's bloodiest tragedy, so it is an example of a play.

clue.text: Find hint about slowing in music

indicators.note: about means going around, so the hint word wraps the musical term

parts.note: a ray of hope is a hint of it
rit. is the score abbreviation for ritardando, a slowing down

explanation.surface: Someone discovers a clue about tempo changes in a piece of music.
explanation.walkthrough: Find looks like a verb, but it is the noun: a valuable discovery.
explanation.definitionFit: A find, as a noun, is a lucky discovery, and something uncommon and prized is called this.

clue.text: Vehicle used by mum takes dad to Paris — not the centre

indicators.note: the middle letter of the Trojan king's name is dropped

parts.note: in Greek legend Priam, king of Troy, was the father of Paris

explanation.surface: A mother's car carries her father to the French capital, avoiding the city centre.
explanation.walkthrough: Paris here is the Trojan prince, not the French city.
explanation.definitionFit: A baby carriage pushed by a mother is called a pram in Britain, the short form of perambulator.

clue.text: Ruler from east, in main Bible parts, depicted in crown

indicators.note: all of that is shown inside the head word

parts.note: pate is the crown of the head

indicators.note: the compass letter goes in between the two testaments

parts.note: the Bible's two main parts are the OT and NT, Old and New Testaments
E is the compass abbreviation for east

explanation.surface: A monarch from the East is portrayed in scriptural scenes inside a crown.
explanation.walkthrough: Crown suggests royalty, but it is the top of the head: PATE takes OTENT inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A potentate is a monarch or other ruler holding great power.

clue.text: Mister Solo shot after a little hesitation

indicators.note: the rearranged letters come after the other pieces

parts.note: a little is just a single letter, A
er is the sound of someone hesitating

indicators.note: shot as in broken or ruined, so these four letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Mr Solo, perhaps Napoleon of TV spy fame, is shot after a moment's pause.
explanation.walkthrough: Mister reads as a title for Mr Solo, but it is something that produces mist.
explanation.definitionFit: A spray can turning liquid into a fine mist is literally a mister, one that mists.

clue.text: Injury brings member to hospital

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hospital, as on road signs
a limb such as an arm is a member of the body

explanation.surface: A wound sends someone to hospital with a limb to be treated.
explanation.definitionFit: Harm is damage or hurt done to someone, the same as an injury.

clue.text: Valued works deconstructing tree ritual

indicators.note: deconstructing means taking apart, so these letters are pulled apart and reassembled

explanation.surface: Prized writings take apart some arboreal ceremony, like academic critics.
explanation.walkthrough: Deconstructing is the literary-theory term, apt for the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Written works esteemed for their artistic merit are collectively known by this term.

clue.text: Including two old pennies in silver cases

indicators.note: the silver letters case, or enclose, the rest

parts.note: Ag is the chemical symbol for silver
d was the abbreviation for a penny before British decimal currency, so two are DD

explanation.surface: A couple of old coins are enclosed in silver containers.
explanation.definitionFit: To say 'adding X' is to say 'including X' too, both putting something extra into a total.

clue.text: Blasphemous worship involving anti-Mass?

indicators.note: involving in the sense of tangling up, so the letters are mixed

explanation.surface: An irreverent cult whose rites oppose the Catholic Mass.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits that the anagram of ANTIMASS also describes the creed.
explanation.definitionFit: Devil worship is regarded by Christians as the ultimate blasphemy.

clue.text: Fugitive ahead perplexed hunter

parts.note: to go on is to go ahead

indicators.note: perplexed means confused, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: An escapee keeps in front of a baffled pursuer.
explanation.definitionFit: A fugitive is someone fleeing capture, an idiom for which is being on the move from the law.

clue.text: Obscure milieu for a Greek tormented by nightmares

indicators.note: a milieu is a surrounding environment, so the obscure word surrounds the rest

parts.note: obscure as a verb or adjective means concealed from view

explanation.surface: A Greek lost in some murky setting suffers bad dreams.
explanation.definitionFit: Being ridden by a hag, a witch thought to sit on sleepers, is to be plagued by bad dreams or worries.

clue.text: Cutter crossing lake seen in Turner

indicators.note: the cutter word spans across the lake letter, which sits within it

parts.note: an axe is a cutting tool
L is the map abbreviation for lake

explanation.surface: A boat crosses water in a painting by J. M. W. Turner.
explanation.walkthrough: Turner suggests the painter of seascapes; it is anything that turns.
explanation.definitionFit: The rod on which a wheel rotates is literally something that turns.

clue.text: Killer shows when to commit offence with donkey

parts.note: an ass is a donkey
as can mean when, as in 'as I left'
to sin is to commit an offence against moral law

explanation.surface: A murderer reveals when to break the law with a donkey's help.
explanation.definitionFit: An assassin is a killer, specifically one who murders a prominent person.

clue.text: Somehow obtain pounds kept in purse

indicators.note: the money letter is kept inside the purse word

parts.note: a bag such as a handbag is a purse
L is the abbreviation for pounds sterling, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: Cash acquired by dubious means is tucked into a handbag.
explanation.definitionFit: Blag is British slang for getting something free by talking one's way into it, by bluff.

clue.text: Say Mr Bloom takes poodle out by lake

indicators.note: by means next to, so the lake letter sits beside the anagram

parts.note: L is the map abbreviation for lake

indicators.note: out as in in disarray, so the dog's letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: A man walks a poodle beside a lake.
explanation.walkthrough: Leopold Bloom is the hero of Joyce's Ulysses; 'Say' marks him as one example of the name.
explanation.definitionFit: Joyce's hero in Ulysses bears this first name, so he is one person so called.

clue.text: Healthy-sounding vegetable chopped for tea

indicators.note: sounding means the word is said aloud and spelt differently

parts.note: rosy cheeks suggest good health

indicators.note: chopped means cut short, losing its final letter

parts.note: a leek is a vegetable

explanation.surface: A wholesome-seeming cut vegetable is prepared for an afternoon meal.
explanation.walkthrough: Rosie Lee is Cockney rhyming slang for tea, the drink.
explanation.definitionFit: In Cockney rhyming slang the name rhymes with the drink and stands for it.

clue.text: Close match leading to drama

parts.note: the close of something is its end
a match is a game

explanation.surface: A tight contest builds up to theatrics.
explanation.walkthrough: Close looks like an adjective, as in a tight match, but it is the noun meaning end.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the title of Samuel Beckett's play, so it is an example of a stage drama.

clue.text: Princess is no spring chicken — last in line

parts.note: someone who is no spring chicken is no longer young

indicators.note: last in picks the final letter of the word that follows

explanation.surface: A royal daughter, no longer young, waits at the back of a queue.
explanation.definitionFit: The Irish princess of the Tristan legend and Wagner's opera bears this name.

clue.text: Marooned family runs round, about to collect scraps

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

indicators.note: the round and about letters collect, or take in, the scraps word

parts.note: O is round in shape
on means about, as in a book on birds
to bin something is to scrap it, so scraps is bins

explanation.surface: A shipwrecked household runs around, about to gather leftovers.
explanation.walkthrough: The Swiss Family Robinson were castaways on a desert island.
explanation.definitionFit: In Wyss's novel the Swiss Family Robinson are shipwrecked on an island, so they are a castaway household.

clue.text: Female graduate rejected an American barman

indicators.note: rejected means sent back, so the two letters are reversed

parts.note: an MA is a Master of Arts graduate
a DA is a District Attorney, an American lawyer called to the bar

explanation.surface: A woman graduate turned down an American bartender.
explanation.walkthrough: A barman here is a lawyer of the bar, not someone serving drinks.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a woman's given name, so the bearer is a female.

clue.text: Couple that's last to abandon fashionable mission

indicators.note: the final pair of letters of the fashion phrase are removed

parts.note: a la mode means in fashion

explanation.surface: The newest pair of partners leave a trendy church outpost.
explanation.definitionFit: The Alamo in Texas was originally a Spanish Catholic mission before its famous siege.

clue.text: Valuable metal one keeps secure for blonde

parts.note: gold is a precious metal
the Roman numeral for one is I
to lock something is to secure it

explanation.surface: Someone safeguards precious bullion on behalf of a fair-haired person.
explanation.definitionFit: The fairy-tale girl who visits the three bears is famous for her fair hair.

clue.text: Notice alpha male — that's first man

parts.note: an ad, an advertisement, is a notice
alpha is the first Greek letter, our A

explanation.surface: Spot the dominant male: he's the one who arrived first.
explanation.walkthrough: Alpha male reads as one phrase but splits into A and M.
explanation.definitionFit: In Genesis he is the first human being God created.

clue.text: Supreme creator's party over at home

indicators.note: over means turned over, so the party word is reversed

parts.note: a do is a party
in means at home, as in staying in

explanation.surface: The supreme deity's celebration is finished, back at his residence.
explanation.definitionFit: In Norse myth he is the chief god, who shaped the world.

clue.text: Where one is distressed in general

indicators.note: distressed means damaged or upset, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A puzzle over where a person feels troubled overall.
explanation.walkthrough: General looks like an adjective; it is the military rank.
explanation.definitionFit: Dwight Eisenhower was a five-star American general before he became president.
